{"metadata":{"description":"DeepSeek Harness plugin for content-aware PDF reading by vision models","id":"gh:1346064150","install_available":true,"language":"Python","name":"dsh-pdf-reader","slug":"AngelosZou/dsh-pdf-reader","topics":["dsh-plugin","dsh-plugins"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DeepSeek Harness plugin for content-aware PDF reading by vision models"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-pdf-reader"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"> DeepSeek Harness plugin for **content-aware PDF reading by vision models**."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"The plugin reads a PDF the way its content demands: text-heavy pages are
extracted as text, while fi"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"gures, tables, formula-heavy or two-column pages are
rendered as high-DPI region crops fed to the vi"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"sion model — so a paper's vector
figures and structured tables are never lost to the per-image token"},{"id":"p4s4","text":"l — so a paper's vector
figures and structured tables are never lost to the per-image token ceiling."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Backed by **PyMuPDF**. When Python or a dependency is missing, the tools return a
clear, actionable "},{"id":"p5s2","text":"warning (with the exact install command) for the agent to
resolve, instead of failing hard."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Requires a Python interpreter with `pymupdf`."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"After installing Python, you can install the
dsh-python-env plugin in DeepSeek
Harness so the agent "},{"id":"p9s2","text":"handles the dependency automatically — it will create a
project venv and install `pymupdf` itself, w"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"ith no manual steps:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"To set it up by hand instead:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"## Tools"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"| Tool | What it does |"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| `pdf_scan` | Per-page content profile — columns, figures (vector regions), raster images, tables, "},{"id":"p15s2","text":"text characters, hasGraphics, formulaRisk, hasTextLayer. Use first to decide how each page should be"},{"id":"p15s3","text":" read. |
| `pdf_read_page` | Read one page. `mode=mixed` is the one-shot: a low-res `fullPage` previ"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"ew + the page text + every auto-detected figure/table region as high-DPI PNGs (paths, cached in `.ds"},{"id":"p15s5","text":"h-pdf-reader`). `mode=auto`/`text`/`render` force a single path. |
| `pdf_render_region` | Targeted "},{"id":"p15s6","text":"high-res render of a `[x0,y0,x1,y1]` region at budget-filling DPI (or an explicit `dpi`), returning "},{"id":"p15s7","text":"its path for `read_image`. |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"## Recommended workflow"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The tools are built around a **preview → content → refine** loop so large PDFs
stay cheap and no lay"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"out is lost to flattening:"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"1. **Preview (whole page, low-res).** Call `pdf_read_page --mode mixed` for a page.
It returns a low"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"-res **`fullPage`** render (the whole layout — formulas, table
gridlines, figure placement, two-colu"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"mn order) plus the page's **text**. Look at
the preview to see *what* is on the page before spending"},{"id":"p18s4","text":" high-res budget on it.
2. **Content (auto, cached).** The same `mixed` call auto-detects every figu"},{"id":"p18s5","text":"re and
table region and renders each as a high-DPI PNG. All PNGs are written to
**`<cwd>/.dsh-pdf-re"},{"id":"p18s6","text":"ader`** and returned **only as paths** — heavy/long content
lives in the cache, never inlined into y"},{"id":"p18s7","text":"our context. Feed the paths to
`read_image`.
3. **Refine (on demand).** If a specific area is still "},{"id":"p18s8","text":"too small, or was not
auto-cropped (an uncropped formula, a crowded table cell, a sub-figure), zoom "},{"id":"p18s9","text":"it
with `pdf_render_region` on the exact `[x0,y0,x1,y1]` you read off the `fullPage`
preview."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Start any document with `pdf_scan` (whole-document overview) to plan which pages
are text-only vs fi"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"gure/table/formula-rich, then apply the loop per page."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## Why this design"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"A two-column paper's **figures are usually vector** (only page rasterization can
see them), **tables"},{"id":"p21s2","text":" lose structure under text extraction**, and **formulas garble**
in some text layers. Meanwhile Deep"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"Seek caps each image at ~**800×800-equivalent /
384 tokens** — so reading a whole two-column page at"},{"id":"p21s4","text":" that budget makes each column
~350px and loses small text, sub/superscripts and figure detail. The "},{"id":"p21s5","text":"t budget makes each column
~350px and loses small text, sub/superscripts and figure detail. The fix:"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"- **Text pages → extraction** (cheap, precise, preserves prose + inline math that
PyMuPDF decodes we"},{"id":"p22s2","text":"ll).
- **Figure/table/math pages → render the region** and scale it to fill the
~640k-pixel budget v"},{"id":"p22s3","text":"ia `dpi = 72 × sqrt(640000 / region_pt_area)`. Content is
complete (nothing legible is lost inside t"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"he budget) and token-optimal
(rendered AT the budget, not beyond it)."},{"id":"p23s1","text":"Region detection is heuristic (not a perfect classifier) and deliberately biased
toward rendering — "},{"id":"p23s2","text":"vector clusters from `get_drawings()`, raster rects from
`get_image_rects()`, the same clustering fo"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"r tables, and math from fonts + a LaTeX
producer. It over-flags (a ruled table or a logo may be trea"},{"id":"p23s4","text":"ted as a figure) rather
than under-flagging, because rendering is cheap and safe."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"## When dependencies are missing"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"Each tool resolves a Python interpreter in priority order — the activated venv
(`$VIRTUAL_ENV`) firs"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"t, then PATH `python`/`python3`/`py`, then the project
`.venv`/`venv`/`env` — probes it for `pymupdf"},{"id":"p25s3","text":"` (and optionally `pymupdf4llm`), and
picks the first one that can import it. If none can, it return"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"s a warning naming
what is missing and how to fix it, so the agent can install the dependency,
switc"},{"id":"p25s5","text":"h interpreters, or fall back."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"## Limitations"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"- **`page.find_tables()` false-positives** on plot grids and diagrams, so tables
are primarily read "},{"id":"p27s2","text":"by rendering (the reliable path); Markdown tables from
`pymupdf4llm` are a best-effort extra.
- Form"},{"id":"p27s3","text":"ula detection is heuristic (fonts + LaTeX producer). PyMuPDF decodes inline
math well, but stacked f"},{"id":"p27s4","text":"ractions can still be imperfect — use
`pdf_render_region` on an equation when exact structure is nee"},{"id":"p27s5","text":"ded.
- A whole page renders to only ~83 DPI-equivalent at the budget; the tools never
do that for a "},{"id":"p27s6","text":"two-column page — they crop regions instead, and body text uses
extraction.
- Large PDFs are parsed "},{"id":"p27s7","text":"age — they crop regions instead, and body text uses
extraction.
- Large PDFs are parsed into memory."},{"id":"p28s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p29s1","text":"- Node ≥ 20, `@deepseek-ai/cordis` ^4, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (peer deps,
provided by the harness)"},{"id":"p29s2","text":".
- Python 3 + `pymupdf` (optional `pymupdf4llm`)."},{"id":"p30s1","text":"## License"},{"id":"p31s1","text":"MIT"}],"truncated":false}
